report_name: Shropshire Local Cycling & Walking Infrastructure Plan
how_pct_was_used: The PCT was used to highlight routes currently used by commuter cyclists and to forecast the number of commuter cyclists on these routes under the government target to double cycling at a national level. The model also accounted for local socio-economic and demographic factors impacting cycling levels in Shropshire.
other_tools_developed: Effectiveness & Needs Based Appraisal and Deliverability metrics
specific_evidence_of_impact: The LCWIP has produced a number of schemes and network upgrades, which must be prioritized over a ten-year period. The top ten scoring schemes, with a mix of short, medium, and long-term delivery timelines, are identified across Oswestry, Shrewsbury, and Ludlow. The LCWIP will support the case for funding for further stages of design, assessment, and stakeholder engagement and consultation, and has led to the integration of LCWIP proposals and key principles within the emerging Shropshire LTP4 and the ongoing planning of highway improvements and new developments. It also influenced future travel plans and identified various funding mechanisms for implementation.
pct_usage_quote: Propensity to Cycle Tool (PCT): This tool uses data from the 2011 Census to highlight routes which are currently used by  commuter cyclists. The PCT was also used to forecast  the number of commuter cyclists on these routes under the government target (as set out in the Second Cycling and Walking Investment Strategy) to double cycling at a national level. The model accounts for the local socio-economic and demographic factors which may impact cycling levels in Shropshire, including the notably higher proportion of older people living in Shropshire (25% of the population is aged over 65 compared to 19% of the population for the West Midlands and England as a whole)
